gum_standard_uncertainty — SPC uncertainty op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.gum_standard_uncertainty(table, halfwidth='halfwidth', distribution='distribution') (to call the implementation directly, import spc; spc.gum_standard_uncertainty(table, halfwidth='halfwidth', distribution='distribution'); from the registry, opsspc.get("gum_standard_uncertainty"))

Usage

Convert uncertainty components from the shape of their distribution into standard uncertainties (table).

What a calibration certificate or standard gives is a form like "half-width a" or "±U at 95 %", not a standard deviation. The propagation law can only consume standard uncertainties, so they are aligned here:

rectangular (uniform) u = a / sqrt(3) triangular u = a / sqrt(6)

U-shaped (arcsine) u = a / sqrt(2) normal_95 u = a / 1.959964

★ Each is an exact value following from the definition of the distribution's variance; taking the sample standard deviation by Monte Carlo converges to the same number (gum_monte_carlo checks it independently).

★★ No default distribution is set. Making rectangular the default because it is used most often would mean a component whose shape was forgotten silently becomes a/sqrt(3) -- if triangular was meant it is off by 1.41x, if a 95 % interval was meant by 1.13x, and that uncertainty flows downstream without an exception.
